newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Rate rise talk dominates short stg trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Rate rise talk dominates short stg trade.

text.p: Speculation that British interest rates may be raised by more than the expected 25 basis points was circulating in the short sterling options pit on Monday, but traders said implied volatility remains immured for the time being.

Britain's monetary policy committee, which sets interest rates, meets on Wednesday and Thursday. The committee has raised British base rates by three successive 25 basis-point moves since May, taking rates to 6.75 percent.

"The market is discounting a quarter-point rise, but there are some aggressive guys going for 50 basis points," said Luke White, options broker at Fimat Futures in London. "But 50 is too much too fast."
He said there was more nervousness in the market about the size of the move, but it had not been sufficient to knock volatility out of its downward range.
December short sterling options on December short sterling futures were trading at 8.75 percent, up from 8.4 percent, while March options were unchanged at 9.9 percent.

December short sterling futures were trading down two basis points at 92.49 while March was also down two at 92.49. Traders noted that the short sterling strip is discounting money market rates of around 7.5 percent out to March 1998.
Over the last few sessions, put buying has dominated, although there was notable call activity in the back months.
So far in Monday's session, one house was noted buying 500 of the 92.00/92.50 short sterling put spread.
A trader at a British brokerage said that the short sterling market was perhaps "too complacent".

"It's like no-one's really expecting anything other than 25 basis points to go on rates," he said. "People betting on 50 are only doing it as a long shot because they'll make a lot of money and it's quite a cheap trade."
White said volatility would squeeze higher if rates were left on hold. He said December would head for 10.0 percent, while March would eye 10.5 percent.
Meantime, a rise of 50 basis points would probably not ignite a major move in volatility until after the next economic data release, which would serve to support or condemn such a move.
"The market would just think that the committee knew something we didn't," said White.

A report out from British bank Barclays overnight said that interest rates should rise to 8.0 percent by early next year to avoid the UK suffering the problems of a volatile growth and inflation cycle.

Elsewhere, in Bund options, trade was sluggish after locals were short of volatility, and unwilling to gamma trade with the underlying futures contract. Some 400 lots of the September straddle traded, at a volatility of around 5.4 percent. Another 400 lot straddle was traded in October at a volatility of 5.4 percent, and a 150 lot straddle was done in November at 5.3 percent.
